summary.one_liner: Tracked down and fixed a Node.js memory leak in a background job processor caused by uncleaned event listener registrations
summary.problem_statement: A long-running job processor service was consuming 600 MB of RAM after 48 hours and eventually OOMing. CloudWatch alarms fired every 2–3 days, requiring a manual restart. The leak had been open for 6 weeks with no one able to reproduce it locally.
summary.approach: Enabled --expose-gc and took heap snapshots with clinic.js before and after each job cycle. Identified that EventEmitter instances from a third-party queue client were accumulating in the retainedSize tree — each job run registered a new 'data' listener on a shared stream without ever removing it. Added explicit removeListener calls in the job teardown path and introduced a weak-ref pattern for the shared stream reference.

tradeoffs.reasoning: clinic.js flame/bubbleprof output is faster to interpret under time pressure — readable in a browser rather than loading a 200 MB .heapsnapshot into Chrome DevTools
tradeoffs.alternative_considered: Manual heap snapshot loop via v8 module — more portable but slower to iterate

tradeoffs.decision: removeListener at job teardown over using once() for initial registration
tradeoffs.reasoning: The listener needed to persist across sub-operations within a job; once() would have fired prematurely. Explicit teardown is more defensive for future callers who might reuse the stream.
tradeoffs.alternative_considered: Refactoring to once() — simpler but would require restructuring the job lifecycle significantly

dead_ends: Suspected a circular reference in the job payload serialization — added JSON.stringify depth limiting, no effect
Added --max-old-space-size=512 thinking it was a GC timing issue, confirmed this only delayed OOM, didn't fix it
Attempted to reproduce locally with a tight loop — couldn't trigger it because the leak only accumulated above ~200 concurrent in-flight jobs
